groups.text: It is currently 15 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has vowed to punish those responsible for university exam fraud severely. The announcement comes as the government faces a wave of student protests that have lasted four days, marking one of the most serious crises since Modi began his third term two years ago. He stated on X that nothing is more important than the future of India's youth and promised to accelerate judicial proceedings against those involved in the fraud. Police previously used force to stop tens of thousands of students from reaching Parliament to demand educational reforms. Separately, the UK Competition and Markets Authority has opened an inquiry into a potential merger in the communications sector. The regulator is now seeking views from interested parties regarding the anticipated acquisition of ITV M&E Holdings Limited by Sky UK Limited to determine if the transaction would negatively impact competition within the United Kingdom.

Donald Trump is expanding the U.S. refugee program, but the benefits are limited to white South Africans. The administration cites an unforeseen refugee emergency as the reason for this shift, while people from other global crisis zones remain barred from entry. This policy follows repeated claims by President Trump that South Africa is committing genocide against white farmers. However, the South African government and the UN Human Rights Office have rejected these allegations, noting a lack of statistical evidence for increased crime targeting white citizens. Experts suggest this move aims to undermine South Africa's international moral authority. This tension coincides with Pretoria’s role as one of Israel's sharpest critics, specifically regarding the genocide case filed at the International Court of Justice over Gaza. Consequently, these targeted refugee policies have left relations between the United States and South Africa strained.

The U.S. government has updated a cybersecurity advisory warning that Iranian hackers are targeting industrial control systems from Siemens, Schneider Electric, and Rockwell Automation. Federal agencies report these actors target internet-exposed programmable logic controllers in the energy, water, and government services sectors, using malicious project files to override safe operating parameters. In other tech news, the Raspberry Pi Foundation has expanded its display lineup with a new 10-inch Touch Display 2 priced at 80 dollars. This model features a 24-bit panel with a resolution of 1,200 by 1,920 pixels and ten-point multi-touch capability, though it requires four DSI lines, limiting its compatibility to the Raspberry Pi 5 or Compute Module. Meanwhile, in Indonesia, Professor Charlie Danny Heatubun is being recognized for his two decades of botanical research in Papua. The University of Papua professor has described 50 new palm species, including the zebra palm discovered during an expedition to the Cycloop Mountains.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has vowed stringent punishment for those involved in a leaked exam papers scandal. This promise follows mass student protests that have become one of the biggest challenges to Modi since his 2024 re-election. On Wednesday, thousands of demonstrators led by the social media-driven Cockroach Janta Party rallied in New Delhi, triggering fresh clashes with police. The movement has also seen protesters demanding educational reforms in Mumbai. In a social media post, Modi stated that nothing is more important than the welfare and future of India's youth. To address the fraud, he promised to establish fast-track courts to punish those responsible for the question paper leaks. He warned that anyone attempting to harm the future of the country's youth will not be spared.

The Trump administration is accusing the Chinese lab Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic’s Fable model to create Kimi K3. This accusation comes as Washington reacts to the July 17 launch of the new LLM, which offers frontier-level performance at lower prices. Moonshot AI plans to publish the weights for Kimi K3 on July 27, a move that would allow companies to install and modify the model on their own servers. This open-source strategy from Beijing is already showing results, with Bloomberg reporting that Chinese models now account for 60 percent of token usage by American firms. In a separate environmental crisis, fishers along India’s west coast are struggling with ghost gear in the Arabian Sea. A study in Kerala found that local fishers lose or discard about 21 percent of their gear annually, more than ten times the global average, yet India lacks a systematic way to retrieve these nets.

Ten people are dead after a fire destroyed a family home in a low-income neighborhood of Lima, Peru. The blaze broke out early Wednesday morning in the La Victoria district, where officials say flammable materials and parked electric vehicles caused the flames to spread rapidly. Among the deceased were five adults and five children; two other people were injured. Local media reports indicate that extortionists targeting local businesses started the fire. President-elect Keiko Fujimori visited the ruins of the home on Wednesday, describing the deaths as a terrible massacre. She told reporters that establishing order and security would be her first priority when she takes office next week. Police chief Oscar Arriola said authorities have launched an investigation to determine the exact point of origin and the circumstances surrounding the fire.

In Aizawl, Mizoram, over a thousand young people gathered on July 22 for a "Peaceful Solidarity Protest against the Brutal Regime." The demonstration took place outside Vanapa Hall during heavy rain and humidity, marking a rare occasion where youth protested independently without the guidance of political parties or NGOs. The crowd demanded that Sonam Wangchuk be allowed to continue his movement without restriction, called for the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and sought one crore rupees in compensation for lives lost following the NEET 2026 paper leak. In other news, Microsoft is expanding its Xbox backward compatibility program by bringing four original Xbox titles to PC and handhelds like the ROG Ally. Fuzion Frenzy, Blinx: The Time Sweeper, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge, and Conker: Live and Reloaded are now available on Windows and Game Pass with improved resolution and audio settings.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with rain chances up to 50 percent and temperatures between 17 and 20 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin and birthday: Nils Bauer turns 36, at 14:00, Meeting Aaron, and at 19:00, ️ Greifen and ️ Greifen.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
